text.p: NWE oil products were mixed on Monday, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil was unchanged. Barges traded at $88 fob ARA.
August IPE gas oil slid $1 a tonne to $162.50, pulled lower by losses in crude, and differentials were steady to easier.
Heating oil barges shed 50 cents to talk at flat to 50 cents over the screen. Low sulphur diesel cargoes shed $1 to talk at August IPE $3.75/$4.50.
The naphtha market weakened gradually through the day, having already seen a fairly sharp early decline on a late Friday slump in crude futures values.
A physical deal at $191 CIF NWE and an August swap trade at $186, both in the afternoon, were indicative of a $3-$4 fall since late Friday afternoon.
Gasoline dealers saw a $2 rise in swap values on the day to around $189 for August by late afternoon, while barge values rose $5 on a perceived tight market to reach $190-$192 for July Eurograde.
